front_matter.preface: This academic monograph, Tangkhul Folk Literature, authored by S. Arokianathan and published by Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysore (1982), provides rigorous descriptive linguistic documentation of the Tangkhul Naga language, including acoustic phonetics, tonal phonology, morphological typology, and authentic folktale texts.

chapters.title: Theoretical Framework & Language Profile
chapters.summary: Linguistic classification, field methodology, informant demographics, and phonological framework.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Folk Literature wui research framework: Tangkhul Naga language documentation. Ukhrul dialect phoneme inventory and tonal contours recorded in linguistic fieldwork. Morpheme boundaries and acoustic vowel formant measurements.
chapters.english_translation: Methodological framework of Tangkhul Folk Literature: Systematic documentation of Tangkhul Naga. Ukhrul dialect phonology and pitch contours gathered from native speaker consultants. Morpheme boundaries and acoustic vowel formant analyses.
comprehension_questions: What theoretical framework guided this linguistic study?
Describe the consultant pool for Ukhrul dialect data.

chapters.title: Segmental Phonetics & Tone Pitch Contours
chapters.summary: Consonantal articulation points, vowel length contrasts, and level vs falling tones.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Vowel formants: F1 and F2 acoustic spaces for a, ā, e, ē, i, ī, o, ō, u, ū. Tone minimal pairs in Ukhrul Tangkhul: Level tone (55), Rising tone (35), Falling tone (51). Glottal catch distribution in word-final codas.
chapters.english_translation: Vowel formant measurements for short and long vowel series. Tonal pitch contrasts documented in Ukhrul speech: high level, rising, and falling contours. Phonemic distribution of syllable-final glottal stops.
comprehension_questions: Identify the three primary tone pitch contours in Tangkhul.
How do vowel formants correlate with vowel length?

chapters.title: Morphological Typology & Affixation
chapters.summary: Agglutinative processes, nominal prefix ka-, verbal aspect markers, and directional affixes.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Morphology: Prefix ka- derivations (kaphā, kacham). Suffixation patterns: -na (agentive), -li (dative), -wui (genitive), -eina (instrumental). Directional verb prefixes and causative -sak.
chapters.english_translation: Morphological processes in Tangkhul: Productive nominalization with ka-. Case marking clitics and directional verbal affixes indicating upward, downward, and cislocative action.
grammar_points: Prefixal vs suffixal asymmetries in Tibeto-Burman.
comprehension_questions: Explain the multifunctional role of prefix ka-.
How are directional movements encoded in verbal stems?

chapters.title: Syntax: Clause Structure & Converb Chaining
chapters.summary: SOV sentence structure, subordinate converbs (-da, -laga), and relative clauses.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Syntax: Subject-Object-Verb word order. Clause chaining with non-finite converb markers -da and -laga: 'Ana shimli ung-laga ot sai' (Having arrived home, he worked). Head-final relative clauses.
chapters.english_translation: Syntactic typology: Strict verb-final (SOV) ordering. Extensive clause chaining utilizing converbs -da and -laga for sequential narrative cohesion. Internally-headed and head-final relative clause constructions.
grammar_points: Topic marking vs focus marking in Tangkhul.
comprehension_questions: Diagram a clause-chained sentence in Tangkhul.
How are relative clauses formed in standard syntax?

chapters.title: Linguistic Texts with Interlinear Glosses
chapters.summary: Folktale narrative transcribed with morpheme-by-morpheme glosses and grammatical analysis.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Khararchan text glossing: Thot-kashak-wui wari akha lei. Mi akha-na lui-li va-da ot sa-i. A-wui shim-li kachak kashak sang-laga matha-yei. Gloss: time-ancient-GEN story one exist. person one-AGT field-LOC go-CONV work do-PRES.
chapters.english_translation: Interlinearized folktale specimen: There was once an ancient legend. A person went to the terrace fields and labored. Returning to his home with grain, he rejoiced. Full Leipzig Glossing Rules applied to each morpheme.
grammar_points: Leipzig glossing conventions applied to Tibeto-Burman.
comprehension_questions: Explain the glossing abbreviation AGT and LOC in the sample text.
How is narrative discourse coherence achieved without overt pronouns?

chapters.title: Comprehensive Lexical Root Index & Summary
chapters.summary: Index of analyzed roots, sound correspondence tables, and bibliographic citations.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Lexical Index: Root morphemes indexed with reconstructed Proto-Tibeto-Burman forms. Cognate sets comparing Ukhrul Tangkhul with neighboring Naga and Kuki languages.
chapters.english_translation: Comprehensive morphological index correlating documented Tangkhul lexical roots with comparative Tibeto-Burman cognate sets and phonetic cross-references.
grammar_points: Comparative historical phonology of Naga languages.
comprehension_questions: Cite two Tangkhul lexical items with clear Proto-Tibeto-Burman cognates.
Summarize the primary morphological discoveries of this volume.
